transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. To start, can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brought you in to see me today?

I’m here because I keep hearing voices from the call-light speaker and the hallway vents. They tell me which patient records have been changed—clear as if someone’s standing right next to me, even when the unit is quiet and nobody else hears anything.
How long have you been hearing these voices from the call-light speaker and vents—days, weeks, or longer?
About two months now. It started around when they asked me to help lead the wound-care documentation rollout.

Over these same two months, have you also noticed a significant change in your mood—like feeling extremely sad, hopeless, or empty, or on the other end, unusually energetic, elated, or needing much less sleep than usual?

Some days I feel like I’m finally awake, like I’m meant to fix everything at work. But if my husband or one of the nurses tells me to slow down, I snap at them. It feels like they’re getting in the way of something important.
When you feel that 'finally awake' burst of energy and purpose, how long does it usually last—do you stay that way for most of the day, every day, for a week or more, or does it come and go quickly?
It’s been pretty steady for about two months now, since they asked me to help lead that wound-care documentation rollout.
In the past two months, have you been using any alcohol, recreational drugs, or new medications/supplements—even occasionally?
I’m not sure what would count. I haven’t really noticed anything like that.
Have you heard these voices from the speaker or vents during times when you were not feeling that surge of energy or irritability—like when your mood felt more normal or even low?

No. I never had the voices from the call lights or saw those messages in the charts before this. They started after I got so wound up about the rollout—sleeping less, working all the time, and feeling like I had to fix everything at the facility.
Have you had any recent medical illnesses, head injuries, seizures, or been told you have a condition like thyroid disease, and are you currently being treated for any physical health problems?
I’m not sure. I haven’t noticed anything like that recently.
Over these past two months, have you noticed any confusion, trouble remembering things, or difficulty knowing where you are or what day it is?
I don’t think so. I’ve been able to tell where I am and what day it is.

opening_question.intent: Identify the primary reason for the visit / chief complaint
opening_question.question: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. To start, can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brought you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient exhibits a distinct ~2-month period of elevated, expansive mood with decreased need for sleep, increased goal-directed activity, grandiosity ('meant to fix everything at work'), and irritability when thwarted—core manic symptoms. Concurrent with this mood disturbance, she developed auditory hallucinations (voices from speakers/vents) that are mood-congruent with her grandiose theme (monitoring documentation to 'fix' the facility). Psychotic symptoms emerged only after and alongside the manic symptoms, with no hallucinations during euthymic periods, ruling out a primary psychotic disorder (schizophrenia/schizoaffective) or brief psychotic disorder. No substance use, medical illness, or cognitive impairment identified as an alternative etiology. This pattern—full manic episode with mood-congruent psychotic features—meets criteria for Bipolar I Disorder, current episode manic, severe with psychotic features (F31.2).
